l17-q01.answer: A system whose failures now come with a citation attached
options: Grounding, since the model can now only answer from documents you supplied
A system whose failures now come with a citation attached
Freshness, which is the main benefit and does not depend on evaluation
Lower cost, since retrieved chunks are cheaper than long-context prompts

l17-q02.answer: Models do not read a long context uniformly: accuracy on a fact is worse when it sits in the middle
options: Latency, since a long prompt takes proportionally longer to process before the first token
Models do not read a long context uniformly: accuracy on a fact is worse when it sits in the middle
Truncation, since providers silently drop the oldest tokens once the window is exceeded
The attention mechanism degrades quadratically, so quality falls smoothly with length

l17-q03.answer: The query is placed in the wrong space and nothing raises; pin the model in the index metadata
options: The vector store validates dimensions, so a mismatch is caught only if the dimensions differ; pad the shorter vectors
The query is placed in the wrong space and nothing raises; pin the model in the index metadata
The scores are renormalised per query, which hides the change; disable normalisation to surface it
The index needs rebuilding on every deploy, and the staleness is what degraded retrieval

l17-q04.answer: In chunking, at ingestion; re-ranking cannot recover a split fact
options: In the retriever: a cross-encoder re-ranker will surface both halves and the model can combine them
In chunking, at ingestion; re-ranking cannot recover a split fact
In the generation prompt: instruct the model to combine partial evidence across retrieved chunks
In k: retrieve more chunks so both halves are likely to appear in the context together

l17-q05.answer: When plain dense retrieval already hits recall@k near 1.0, since there is nothing left to improve
options: When the corpus is large, since two indexes do not scale to millions of documents
When plain dense retrieval already hits recall@k near 1.0, since there is nothing left to improve
When queries are short, since re-rankers need long queries to score against
When the embedding model is recent, since modern embeddings subsume what BM25 contributes

l17-q06.answer: That it is topically close, and nothing about whether it answers the question or even agrees with it
options: That the chunk is relevant with roughly 83% confidence, which is a usable threshold
That it is topically close, and nothing about whether it answers the question or even agrees with it
That it is the best match available, since scores are normalised across the corpus
That the answer can be generated from it, provided the score exceeds your tuned cutoff

l17-q07.answer: Build the retrieval gold set and measure recall@k before ever judging a generated answer
options: Judge the generated answers first, since that is what users experience, then trace failures back to retrieval
Build the retrieval gold set and measure recall@k before ever judging a generated answer
Both at once, since retrieval and generation failures are indistinguishable from the outside
Neither in isolation; only end-to-end task success is meaningful for a retrieval system

l17-q09.answer: Exact lexical matching, which is what rescues a query containing a part number or an error code
options: Semantic matching across paraphrase, which embeddings approximate less reliably
Exact lexical matching, which is what rescues a query containing a part number or an error code
A calibrated probability of relevance, which dense scores lack
Language independence, since term statistics do not depend on a trained model

l17-q10.answer: The fraction of questions whose correct chunk appears in the top k
options: The fraction of generated answers that cite a real source, which is the grounding rate
The fraction of questions whose correct chunk appears in the top k
The average similarity of the top k chunks, which indicates whether the index is well built
The fraction of retrieved chunks that are relevant, which is precision at the retrieval stage
